And a voice from heaven says: you are my Son, the Beloved; with you I am well pleased (Mark 1:10–11). Father, Son and Holy Spirit are revealed together.

Isaiah described this Servant long before: here is my servant, whom I uphold, my chosen, in whom my soul delights; I have put my spirit upon him (Isaiah 42:1). He will not break a bruised reed. He will be a light to the nations and open the eyes of the blind.

In the second reading Peter sums up Jesus' whole life in one sentence: God anointed Jesus of Nazareth with the Holy Spirit and with power; he went about doing good and healing all who were oppressed by the devil (Acts 10:38). That anointing began at the Jordan. And Peter says this to a Roman family: the grace of the Jordan is for every nation.
Why was the sinless Jesus baptised? To stand with sinners and to make the waters holy for us. In our Baptism the heavens opened over us too, and the Father said: you are my beloved child.
So today let us renew our baptismal promises with all our heart. Let us find out the date of our Baptism. And let us go about doing good this week, as people anointed by the Spirit. Amen.
kids: Children, today Jesus was baptised in the river. The Holy Spirit came like a dove and God said: you are my beloved Son!
When you were baptised, God said: you are my beloved child. Ask your parents to show you your Baptism photos!

homily: Dear friends, on the second day of the new year the Gospel asks a simple question: who are you? The priests and Levites come to John the Baptist and ask him this. John first says what he is not: I am not the Messiah, not Elijah, not the prophet (John 1:20–21).

Then he says who he is: I am the voice of one crying out in the wilderness, make straight the way of the Lord (John 1:23). A voice exists to carry a word. John knows that his whole life is to carry Christ to others. That is true humility: not hating ourselves, but knowing that we live for someone greater.

St John in the first reading tells us to let what we heard from the beginning abide in us (1 John 2:24). Many voices around us offer a new gospel. The Church asks us to stay with the faith of the Apostles.

Today we remember Saints Basil and Gregory, two friends from Cappadocia in present-day Turkey. They studied together in Athens, prayed together as monks, and became bishops. They defended the truth that Jesus is truly God and that the Holy Spirit is truly God. Gregory said that in Athens they knew only two roads: the road to church and the road to school.
Let us ask for John's humility and for holy friendships like theirs. Let our words and our lives say: not me, but Christ. Amen.
kids: Children, John the Baptist said: I am only a voice; Jesus is the important one! Today let us help someone to know Jesus.

homily: Dear friends, after the Epiphany the Church follows the light as it spreads. Jesus leaves Nazareth and makes his home in Capernaum, by the Sea of Galilee. Matthew calls this region Galilee of the Gentiles, a border land where Jews and pagans lived side by side.

There Isaiah's words come true: the people who sat in darkness have seen a great light (Matthew 4:16). Jesus does not start in Jerusalem, among the important people. He starts on the margins, where people felt far from God.

His first word is: repent, for the kingdom of heaven has come near (Matthew 4:17). To repent means to turn around. God has come close; we must turn to face him. Then Jesus heals every disease and sickness, and crowds come from everywhere.

St John warns us to test the spirits (1 John 4:1). Not every voice that speaks of God leads to God. The test is simple: does it confess Jesus Christ come in the flesh? Does it lead to the Church, the sacraments, love of neighbour?
Let us welcome the light today. Let us turn from one thing that keeps us in darkness. And let us take courage: the one who is in you is greater than the one who is in the world (1 John 4:4). Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus is like a big light that came to people who were in the dark. When we say sorry and do good, we let his light shine in us!

homily: Dear friends, St John today writes the most famous sentence of his letter: God is love (1 John 4:8). Not only does God love; love is what God is, from all eternity: Father, Son and Holy Spirit.

And John tells us where we can see this love: in this is love, not that we loved God but that he loved us and sent his Son (1 John 4:10). Our love is always a reply. Before we ever prayed, God loved us.

In the Gospel Jesus sees a great crowd and has compassion for them, because they are like sheep without a shepherd (Mark 6:34). He first teaches them, feeding their minds and hearts. Then evening comes and they are hungry.

The disciples say: send them away. Jesus says: you give them something to eat (Mark 6:37). They have only five loaves and two fish. Jesus takes them, looks up to heaven, blesses, breaks and gives. Five thousand eat and twelve baskets are left over. Our little in his hands becomes enough.
These are the words of the Last Supper and of every Mass: took, blessed, broke, gave. Let us bring our five loaves today, our time, our money, our talents, and let him multiply them for others. Amen.
kids: Children, a boy gave Jesus five loaves and two fish, and Jesus fed thousands of people! When you share, Jesus can do great things with your little gift.

homily: Dear friends, Jesus returns to Galilee filled with the power of the Spirit, and on the sabbath he goes to the synagogue of Nazareth, as was his custom (Luke 4:14–16). He is handed the scroll of the prophet Isaiah.

He reads: the Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he has anointed me to bring good news to the poor, to proclaim release to the captives and recovery of sight to the blind, to let the oppressed go free (Luke 4:18). Then he sits down, and every eye is fixed on him.

And he says: today this scripture has been fulfilled in your hearing (Luke 4:21). Not one day in the future, not only in the past: today. The word of God is alive. When we hear it at Mass, Christ himself is speaking to us.

St John adds: we love because he first loved us. Those who say, I love God, and hate their brothers or sisters, are liars (1 John 4:19–20). The programme of Nazareth, good news to the poor, freedom for captives, must become our programme.

Today we remember St Raymond of Penyafort, who helped ransom Christian captives and spent his life as a confessor, setting sinners free. May the word of God be fulfilled today in us, in love for the poor and in peace with our brothers and sisters. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus read from the Bible and said: today God's promise comes true! When we help the poor and are kind, God's word comes true in us too.

homily: Dear friends, in one of the towns a man covered with leprosy sees Jesus, falls on his face and begs: Lord, if you choose, you can make me clean (Luke 5:12). He does not doubt Jesus' power. He only asks whether Jesus wants to.

Jesus answers first with his hand. He stretches it out and touches him. By the Law, touching a leper made a person unclean. But with Jesus the opposite happens: his holiness flows into the sick man. I do choose. Be made clean (Luke 5:13). Immediately the leprosy leaves him.
Then Jesus sends him to the priest. Healing is not only for the body; the man must be restored to his family and his community. God's mercy always brings us back to belonging.

Luke adds that crowds came to hear and be healed, but Jesus would withdraw to deserted places and pray (Luke 5:16). St John tells us that God has given us eternal life in his Son; whoever has the Son has life (1 John 5:11–12). In Baptism and the Eucharist, the water and the blood, Jesus still touches us.
What is the leprosy you are ashamed to bring to Jesus? Bring it to him in confession. He still says: I do choose. Be made clean. Amen.
kids: Children, nobody wanted to touch the sick man, but Jesus did! Let us be kind to children whom others leave alone.

homily: Dear friends, the disciples of John the Baptist come to him upset: the one you baptised is baptising, and all are going to him (John 3:26). They feel their master is losing out.

John answers with great freedom. No one can receive anything except what has been given from heaven. Then he uses a wedding image: the bride belongs to the bridegroom. The friend of the bridegroom stands and hears him and rejoices greatly at his voice (John 3:29). John is the best man, not the groom.

And he says the sentence that sums up his life: he must increase, but I must decrease (John 3:30). Jealousy is one of the great sicknesses of parishes, families and workplaces. John shows the cure: joy that Christ is loved, even if I am forgotten.

St John's letter ends with confidence and a warning. If we ask anything according to his will, he hears us (1 John 5:14). And: little children, keep yourselves from idols (1 John 5:21). An idol is anything that takes God's place, including my own importance.
Tomorrow we celebrate the Baptism of the Lord, when John baptises Jesus in the Jordan. Let us prepare by letting Christ grow larger in our lives, and our pride grow smaller. Amen.
kids: Children, John the Baptist was happy when people loved Jesus more than him. Let us be happy when our friends do well!

homily: Dear friends, today Ordinary Time begins. It is called ordinary not because it is dull, but because its weeks are numbered in order. It is the time to follow Jesus through his public life.

Hebrews begins with a solemn sentence: long ago God spoke to our ancestors in many and various ways by the prophets, but in these last days he has spoken to us by a Son (Hebrews 1:1–2). The prophets were many voices; the Son is the final Word. He is the reflection of God's glory and the exact imprint of God's very being.
Mark gives us Jesus' first preaching: the time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God has come near; repent, and believe in the good news (Mark 1:15). God's time has arrived. We must turn and trust.

Then Jesus walks by the lake and sees Simon and Andrew casting nets, James and John mending nets. Follow me and I will make you fish for people (Mark 1:17). Immediately they leave their nets. Jesus calls them in the middle of their ordinary work.
In these ordinary weeks, let us listen to the Son and let go of one net that holds us back. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus called fishermen to follow him, and they went right away! Jesus calls you too. How will you follow him today?

homily: Dear friends, Jesus enters the synagogue of Capernaum and teaches. The people are astounded, for he taught them as one having authority, and not as the scribes (Mark 1:22). The scribes quoted others; Jesus speaks in his own name.

Suddenly a man with an unclean spirit shouts: I know who you are, the Holy One of God. Jesus rebukes the spirit: be silent, and come out of him! And the man is set free. Jesus' word does not only inform; it transforms.

Hebrews looks at Psalm 8: what are human beings that you are mindful of them? God crowned us with glory, yet we see so much broken. But we do see Jesus, who for a little while was made lower than the angels, now crowned with glory and honor because of the suffering of death (Hebrews 2:9).

And he is not ashamed to call us brothers and sisters (Hebrews 2:11). The one who commands evil spirits is our brother. Let his word have authority in our lives today, and let us trust him to set us free. Amen.
kids: Children, when Jesus spoke, even evil had to obey! Jesus is very strong, and he is also our brother who loves us.

homily: Dear friends, today's Gospel shows us a full day in the life of Jesus. After teaching in the synagogue he goes to Simon's house, where Simon's mother-in-law is in bed with a fever.

He came and took her by the hand and lifted her up. Then the fever left her, and she began to serve them (Mark 1:31). The first thing she does with her new strength is serve. Healing leads to service.

At sunset the whole town gathers at the door, and Jesus cures many. Then: in the morning, while it was still very dark, he got up and went out to a deserted place, and there he prayed (Mark 1:35). Jesus' busy day rests on his night prayer.

Hebrews tells us why he came so close: he became like us in every respect, so that he might be a merciful and faithful high priest. Because he himself was tested by what he suffered, he is able to help those who are being tested (Hebrews 2:18).
Today we remember St Hilary, who defended faith in Christ even in exile. Let us ask for Jesus' habit of early prayer, and let him lift us up to serve. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus prayed very early in the morning, while it was still dark. Tomorrow, say a little prayer to Jesus as soon as you wake up!

homily: Dear friends, Hebrews quotes Psalm 95 with great urgency: today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts (Hebrews 3:7–8). The people in the wilderness saw God's works for forty years and still turned away. A heart can harden slowly, without noticing.

The remedy is community: exhort one another every day, as long as it is called today, so that none of you may be hardened by the deceitfulness of sin (Hebrews 3:13). We need each other to stay soft toward God.

In the Gospel a leper kneels before Jesus: if you choose, you can make me clean. Mark says Jesus was moved with pity, a compassion felt deep inside. He stretched out his hand and touched him: I do choose. Be made clean! (Mark 1:41).

Then something surprising happens. The healed man tells everyone, and Jesus could no longer go into a town openly, but stayed out in the country (Mark 1:45). The leper goes back into society; Jesus takes his place outside. That is what Jesus does for us all the way to the Cross.

In India today many honour St Devasahayam, who after his Baptism refused to treat anyone as untouchable and gave his life for Christ. Let us hear the Lord's voice today, keep our hearts soft, and love across every barrier. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus felt so sorry for the sick man that he touched him and made him well. Let us be kind to anyone who is left out.

homily: Dear friends, the house in Capernaum is packed. Four men arrive carrying a paralysed friend on a mat. They cannot get near Jesus. So they climb the roof, dig through it and lower their friend right in front of Jesus.
Mark says: when Jesus saw their faith (Mark 2:5). The faith of the friends matters. We are saved as a people, carried by others' prayers and love.

Then Jesus says something unexpected: son, your sins are forgiven. He sees the deepest paralysis. The scribes think: who can forgive sins but God alone? They are right about God. They do not see that God is standing in front of them.
To show his authority, Jesus says: stand up, take your mat and go. And the man walks out before them all. Everyone says: we have never seen anything like this! (Mark 2:12).

Hebrews invites us: let us make every effort to enter God's rest (Hebrews 4:11). Forgiveness is the door. Let us go to confession, and let us be the four friends for someone who cannot reach Jesus alone. Amen.
kids: Children, four friends carried a sick man to Jesus, even through a roof! Jesus forgave him and made him walk. Can you bring a friend to Jesus by praying for them?

homily: Dear friends, Hebrews gives us a strong image: the word of God is living and active, sharper than any two-edged sword; it is able to judge the thoughts and intentions of the heart (Hebrews 4:12). God's word sees us as we are.

That could frighten us. But Hebrews continues: we do not have a high priest who is unable to sympathize with our weaknesses, but one who in every respect has been tested as we are, yet without sin. Let us therefore approach the throne of grace with boldness (Hebrews 4:15–16).
In the Gospel Jesus sees Levi at the tax booth. Tax collectors worked for the Romans and were often dishonest. People despised them. Jesus simply says: follow me. And Levi gets up and follows.

Then Jesus eats at Levi's house with many tax collectors and sinners. The Pharisees complain. Jesus says: those who are well have no need of a physician, but those who are sick; I have come to call not the righteous but sinners (Mark 2:17).

The Church is a hospital for sinners. Let God's word show us our sickness, and let us come boldly to the throne of grace for healing. On this Saturday let us also ask Mary, Refuge of sinners, to bring us to her Son. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus called Levi, whom nobody liked, to be his friend. Jesus loves everyone. Let us be friends with someone who has no friends.

intro: Theme: “Born of a woman, so that we might be children of God.”
Mary's divine motherhood, our adoption, and God's blessing for the new year.

sub: The child is the eternal Son.
Honouring Mary protects the truth about Jesus.
q: Therefore the Lord himself will give you a sign. Look, the young woman is with child and shall bear a son, and shall name him Immanuel.
And why has this happened to me, that the mother of my Lord comes to me?
points.apply: Pray the Hail Mary slowly today, weighing the words “Mother of God”.

sub: Born under the law to redeem us.
q: As a mother comforts her child, so I will comfort you; you shall be comforted in Jerusalem.
But when the fullness of time had come, God sent his Son, born of a woman, born under the law, in order to redeem those who were under the law, so that we might receive adoption as children.
points.apply: Begin each prayer this week with the word “Abba, Father”.

q: The LORD bless you and keep you; the LORD make his face to shine upon you, and be gracious to you; the LORD lift up his countenance upon you, and give you peace.
But Mary treasured all these words and pondered them in her heart.
points.apply: Write one line each night on what God did that day.

concl: Mary gives us Jesus, and Jesus makes us children of the Father.
Let us begin the year with her, blessed and at peace.
2027-01-01.resolve: Bless your family with Numbers 6:24–26 on every first day of the month this year.

intro: Theme: “Nations shall come to your light.”
Christ revealed to the nations; seeking, finding and adoring.

points.h: A light for all the nations
sub: Isaiah's vision of the nations streaming in.
Paul's mystery: the Gentiles are fellow heirs.
q: Arise, shine; for your light has come, and the glory of the LORD has risen upon you.
that is, the Gentiles have become fellow heirs, members of the same body, and sharers in the promise in Christ Jesus through the gospel.
points.apply: Pray for one person who does not yet know Christ.

sub: The scribes know but do not go.
q: Nations shall come to your light, and kings to the brightness of your dawn.
asking, “Where is the child who has been born king of the Jews? For we observed his star at its rising, and have come to pay him homage.”
points.apply: Read one chapter of a Gospel each day this month.

sub: They knelt and paid him homage.
q: May all kings fall down before him, all nations give him service.

When they saw that the star had stopped, they were overwhelmed with joy. On entering the house, they saw the child with Mary his mother; and they knelt down and paid him homage. Then, opening their treasure chests, they offered him gifts of gold, frankincense, and myrrh.
points.apply: Spend fifteen minutes in adoration before the Blessed Sacrament this week.

concl: The star leads to the Child; the Child leads to the Cross and the empty tomb.
Whoever adores Christ cannot go back the same way.
2027-01-03.resolve: Bless your home this week and offer Christ one concrete gift.

intro: Theme: “Take heart, it is I; do not be afraid.”
Christ comes across the storm; love casts out fear.

sub: He sees them in the dark.
q: He will not let your foot be moved; he who keeps you will not slumber. He who keeps Israel will neither slumber nor sleep.
After saying farewell to them, he went up on the mountain to pray.
points.apply: Pray each night this week for those who are struggling.

q: When you pass through the waters, I will be with you; and through the rivers, they shall not overwhelm you; when you walk through fire you shall not be burned, and the flame shall not consume you.
for they all saw him and were terrified. But immediately he spoke to them and said, “Take heart, it is I; do not be afraid.”
points.apply: Repeat “Jesus, I trust in you” when fear rises.

sub: Hearts hardened in spite of signs.
God lives in us when we love.
q: The LORD is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear? The LORD is the stronghold of my life; of whom shall I be afraid?
There is no fear in love, but perfect love casts out fear; for fear has to do with punishment, and whoever fears has not reached perfection in love.
points.apply: Do one act of love toward someone you fear.

concl: The Lord of the sea climbs into our small boat.
Where love lives, fear loses its grip.
2027-01-06.resolve: Pray Psalm 27 each morning this week.

intro: Theme: “You are my Son, the Beloved; with you I am well pleased.”
The Servant anointed at the Jordan, and our Baptism.

sub: He will not break a bruised reed.
q: Here is my servant, whom I uphold, my chosen, in whom my soul delights; I have put my spirit upon him; he will bring forth justice to the nations.
He proclaimed, “The one who is more powerful than I is coming after me; I am not worthy to stoop down and untie the thong of his sandals.
points.apply: Be gentle this week with someone who is fragile.

q: The voice of the LORD is over the waters; the God of glory thunders, the LORD, over mighty waters.
And just as he was coming up out of the water, he saw the heavens torn apart and the Spirit descending like a dove on him.
points.apply: Pray to the Holy Spirit each morning this week.

q: Ho, everyone who thirsts, come to the waters; and you that have no money, come, buy and eat! Come, buy wine and milk without money and without price.
how God anointed Jesus of Nazareth with the Holy Spirit and with power; how he went about doing good and healing all who were oppressed by the devil, for God was with him.
points.apply: Do one deliberate act of kindness each day this week.

sub: We are buried and raised with him.
q: I will sprinkle clean water upon you, and you shall be clean from all your uncleannesses, and from all your idols I will cleanse you.
As many of you as were baptized into Christ have clothed yourselves with Christ.
points.apply: Find your baptismal date and celebrate it this year.

concl: The heavens opened at the Jordan and have not closed.
Live as the Father's beloved, anointed to do good.
2027-01-10.resolve: Renew your baptismal promises today and bless yourself with holy water each day.

intro: Theme: “I am the voice of one crying out in the wilderness.”
John points to Christ; Basil and Gregory defend the faith.

sub: John says what he is not.
He says who he is: a voice.
A voice exists for the Word.
q: A voice cries out: “In the wilderness prepare the way of the LORD, make straight in the desert a highway for our God.”
He said, “I am the voice of one crying out in the wilderness, ‘Make straight the way of the Lord,’” as the prophet Isaiah said.
points.apply: Let one conversation today point to Christ.

sub: Stay with the faith of the Apostles.
q: But this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, says the LORD: I will put my law within them, and I will write it on their hearts; and I will be their God, and they shall be my people.
Let what you heard from the beginning abide in you. If what you heard from the beginning abides in you, then you will abide in the Son and in the Father.
points.apply: Read one paragraph of the Creed in the Catechism this week.

q: For the LORD gives wisdom; from his mouth come knowledge and understanding;
He must increase, but I must decrease.
points.apply: Thank God for a friend who strengthens your faith.

concl: We are voices; Christ is the Word.
Faithful to what we heard, humble like John.
2027-01-02.resolve: Pray the Creed slowly each morning this week.

intro: Theme: “The people who sat in darkness have seen a great light.”
The light moves out into Galilee; conversion and discernment.

sub: God begins where people feel far away.
q: I am the LORD, I have called you in righteousness, I have taken you by the hand and kept you; I have given you as a covenant to the people, a light to the nations, to open the eyes that are blind, to bring out the prisoners from the dungeon, from the prison those who sit in darkness.
the people who sat in darkness have seen a great light, and for those who sat in the region and shadow of death light has dawned.
points.apply: Visit or call someone who lives on the margins of your parish.

q: Cast away from you all the transgressions that you have committed against me, and get yourselves a new heart and a new spirit! Why will you die, O house of Israel?
From that time Jesus began to proclaim, “Repent, for the kingdom of heaven has come near.”
points.apply: Go to confession this month.

sub: Not every voice is from God.
Christ in the flesh is the test.
The one in you is greater.
q: I will tell of the decree of the LORD: He said to me, “You are my son; today I have begotten you.
Little children, you are from God, and have conquered them; for the one who is in you is greater than the one who is in the world.
points.apply: Check one religious message against Church teaching before sharing it.

concl: The light that the Magi saw now walks through Galilee.
Turn to it, and test every other light by it.
2027-01-04.resolve: Read Matthew 4 slowly this evening and pray for those in darkness.

intro: Theme: “God is love.”
The compassion of the Shepherd who feeds his flock.

q: I myself will be the shepherd of my sheep, and I will make them lie down, says the Lord GOD.
As he went ashore, he saw a great crowd; and he had compassion for them, because they were like sheep without a shepherd; and he began to teach them many things.
points.apply: Notice one person in need today before they ask.

points.h: You give them something to eat
sub: The disciples want to send them away.
q: But his servant said, “How can I set this before a hundred people?” So he repeated, “Give it to the people and let them eat, for thus says the LORD, ‘They shall eat and have some left.’”
But he answered them, “You give them something to eat.” They said to him, “Are we to go and buy two hundred denarii worth of bread, and give it to them to eat?”
points.apply: Give food to a family in need this week.

q: the LORD appeared to him from far away. I have loved you with an everlasting love; therefore I have continued my faithfulness to you.
Beloved, let us love one another, because love is from God; everyone who loves is born of God and knows God. Whoever does not love does not know God, for God is love.
points.apply: Thank God tonight for three signs of his love.

concl: The miracle of the loaves continues at every altar.
Love received becomes love shared.
2027-01-05.resolve: Share a meal with someone in need this week.

intro: Theme: “Today this scripture has been fulfilled in your hearing.”
The Anointed One at Nazareth; love of God shown in love of neighbour.

sub: Jesus returns in the power of the Spirit.
He is the Christ, the Anointed.
q: The spirit of the Lord GOD is upon me, because the LORD has anointed me; he has sent me to bring good news to the oppressed, to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives, and release to the prisoners;

“The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he has anointed me to bring good news to the poor. He has sent me to proclaim release to the captives and recovery of sight to the blind, to let the oppressed go free,
points.apply: Pray for those who are poor, captive or blind in our town.

sub: Christ speaks when the Scriptures are read.
q: For he is our God, and we are the people of his pasture, and the sheep of his hand. O that today you would listen to his voice!
Then he began to say to them, “Today this scripture has been fulfilled in your hearing.”
points.apply: Choose one verse from today's readings and live it today.

sub: We love because he first loved us.
No split between God and neighbour.
q: You shall not take vengeance or bear a grudge against any of your people, but you shall love your neighbor as yourself: I am the LORD.
Those who say, “I love God,” and hate their brothers or sisters, are liars; for those who do not love a brother or sister whom they have seen, cannot love God whom they have not seen.
points.apply: Make peace with one person this week.

concl: The programme of Nazareth becomes our programme.
Today, not tomorrow, God's word wants to come true in us.
2027-01-07.resolve: Do one work of mercy for a poor or imprisoned person this month.

intro: Theme: “Lord, if you choose, you can make me clean.”
The touch of Jesus heals and restores; whoever has the Son has life.

sub: The leper believes in Jesus' power.
He asks only about his will.
q: So he went down and immersed himself seven times in the Jordan, according to the word of the man of God; his flesh was restored like the flesh of a young boy, and he was clean.
Once, when he was in one of the cities, there was a man covered with leprosy. When he saw Jesus, he bowed with his face to the ground and begged him, “Lord, if you choose, you can make me clean.”
points.apply: Pray today: Lord, if you choose, heal me.

sub: He restores the man to the community.
q: Surely he has borne our infirmities and carried our diseases; yet we accounted him stricken, struck down by God, and afflicted.
Then Jesus stretched out his hand, touched him, and said, “I do choose. Be made clean.” Immediately the leprosy left him.
points.apply: Visit a sick person whom few people visit.

q: I will sprinkle clean water upon you, and you shall be clean from all your uncleannesses, and from all your idols I will cleanse you.
And this is the testimony: God gave us eternal life, and this life is in his Son. Whoever has the Son has life; whoever does not have the Son of God does not have life.
points.apply: Go to confession and receive the Eucharist with new faith.

concl: Jesus still says: I do choose.
His touch reaches us in the sacraments.
2027-01-08.resolve: Make a good confession before the Baptism of the Lord on Sunday.

intro: Theme: “He must increase, but I must decrease.”
The joy of the Bridegroom's friend; prayer and freedom from idols.

sub: John is the friend who rejoices.
q: For as a young man marries a young woman, so shall your builder marry you, and as the bridegroom rejoices over the bride, so shall your God rejoice over you.
He who has the bride is the bridegroom. The friend of the bridegroom, who stands and hears him, rejoices greatly at the bridegroom's voice. For this reason my joy has been fulfilled.
points.apply: Married couples: renew your vows in prayer together this week.

q: Not to us, O LORD, not to us, but to your name give glory, for the sake of your steadfast love and your faithfulness.
He must increase, but I must decrease.
points.apply: Praise someone whose success you envy.

sub: He hears us when we ask by his will.
Pray for a brother who sins.
q: you shall have no other gods before me.

And this is the boldness we have in him, that if we ask anything according to his will, he hears us. And if we know that he hears us in whatever we ask, we know that we have obtained the requests made of him.
points.apply: Name one idol in your life and give it back to God.

concl: John's joy is complete when Christ is loved.
Let Christ grow, and every idol shrink.
2027-01-09.resolve: Prepare for the Baptism of the Lord by renewing your baptismal promises tonight.

intro: Theme: “The time is fulfilled… repent, and believe in the good news.”
God's final Word in the Son, and the call to follow.

points.h: God has spoken by a Son
q: I will raise up for them a prophet like you from among their own people; I will put my words in the mouth of the prophet, who shall speak to them everything that I command.

Long ago God spoke to our ancestors in many and various ways by the prophets, but in these last days he has spoken to us by a Son, whom he appointed heir of all things, through whom he also created the worlds.
points.apply: Read one chapter of Mark each day this month.

q: And in the days of those kings the God of heaven will set up a kingdom that shall never be destroyed, nor shall this kingdom be left to another people. It shall crush all these kingdoms and bring them to an end, and it shall stand forever;
and saying, “The time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God has come near; repent, and believe in the good news.”
points.apply: Make a good examination of conscience tonight.

q: He left the oxen, ran after Elijah, and said, “Let me kiss my father and my mother, and then I will follow you.” Then Elijah said to him, “Go back again; for what have I done to you?”
And Jesus said to them, “Follow me and I will make you fish for people.” And immediately they left their nets and followed him.
points.apply: Let go of one net that holds you back.

concl: Ordinary Time is the time of following.
The Son speaks; let us listen and follow.
2027-01-11.resolve: Read Mark's Gospel day by day through this season.

intro: Theme: “He taught them as one having authority.”
The word that frees, and the brother crowned with glory.

q: so shall my word be that goes out from my mouth; it shall not return to me empty, but it shall accomplish that which I purpose, and succeed in the thing for which I sent it.
They were astounded at his teaching, for he taught them as one having authority, and not as the scribes.
points.apply: Obey one word of Jesus today.

q: what are human beings that you are mindful of them, mortals that you care for them? Yet you have made them a little lower than God, and crowned them with glory and honor.

but we do see Jesus, who for a little while was made lower than the angels, now crowned with glory and honor because of the suffering of death, so that by the grace of God he might taste death for everyone.
points.apply: Offer one suffering today in union with Jesus.

q: I will tell of your name to my brothers and sisters; in the midst of the congregation I will praise you:
For the one who sanctifies and those who are sanctified all have one Father. For this reason Jesus is not ashamed to call them brothers and sisters,
points.apply: Treat a difficult person today as Jesus' brother or sister.

concl: His word has authority over evil.
He is our brother, crowned with glory.
2027-01-12.resolve: Let one teaching of Jesus shape a concrete decision this week.

intro: Theme: “In the morning, while it was still very dark, he got up… and there he prayed.”
Healing that leads to service, prayer that sustains, a priest who understands.

sub: He takes her by the hand.
q: O LORD my God, I cried to you for help, and you have healed me.
He came and took her by the hand and lifted her up. Then the fever left her, and she began to serve them.
points.apply: Serve someone today in thanks for a blessing.

q: O LORD, in the morning you hear my voice; in the morning I plead my case to you, and watch.
In the morning, while it was still very dark, he got up and went out to a deserted place, and there he prayed.
points.apply: Pray before you touch your phone each morning.

sub: He shared our flesh and blood.
He frees us from the fear of death.
He helps those who are tested.
q: He was despised and rejected by others; a man of suffering and acquainted with infirmity; and as one from whom others hide their faces he was despised, and we held him of no account.
Because he himself was tested by what he suffered, he is able to help those who are being tested.
points.apply: Bring your present trial to Jesus by name.

concl: Jesus' power flows from his prayer.
He who was tested lifts us up to serve.
2027-01-13.resolve: Keep a morning prayer time all this week.

intro: Theme: “Moved with pity, Jesus stretched out his hand and touched him.”
Today's call, the compassion of Jesus, and the One who goes outside for us.

q: Do not harden your hearts, as at Meribah, as on the day at Massah in the wilderness,
But exhort one another every day, as long as it is called “today,” so that none of you may be hardened by the deceitfulness of sin.
points.apply: Encourage one person in faith today.

q: The person who has the leprous disease shall wear torn clothes and let the hair of his head be disheveled; and he shall cover his upper lip and cry out, “Unclean, unclean.”
Moved with pity, Jesus stretched out his hand and touched him, and said to him, “I do choose. Be made clean!”
points.apply: Visit someone who is lonely or excluded.

sub: The healed man spreads the news.
q: But he was wounded for our transgressions, crushed for our iniquities; upon him was the punishment that made us whole, and by his bruises we are healed.
But he went out and began to proclaim it freely, and to spread the word, so that Jesus could no longer go into a town openly, but stayed out in the country; and people came to him from every quarter.
points.apply: Thank Jesus for taking your place.

concl: Today is the day to hear his voice.
Jesus goes outside so that the outcast may come in.
2027-01-14.resolve: Cross one barrier of caste, class or prejudice this week.

intro: Theme: “Son, your sins are forgiven.”
Faith that carries others, forgiveness that heals, rest that God promises.

sub: Four friends dig through the roof.
q: But Ruth said, “Do not press me to leave you or to turn back from following you! Where you go, I will go; where you lodge, I will lodge; your people shall be my people, and your God my God.
When Jesus saw their faith, he said to the paralytic, “Son, your sins are forgiven.”
points.apply: Pray daily this week for one friend far from God.

q: I, I am He who blots out your transgressions for my own sake, and I will not remember your sins.
And he stood up, and immediately took the mat and went out before all of them; so that they were all amazed and glorified God, saying, “We have never seen anything like this!”
points.apply: Go to confession before the end of January.

q: And on the seventh day God finished the work that he had done, and he rested on the seventh day from all the work that he had done.
Let us therefore make every effort to enter that rest, so that no one may fall through such disobedience as theirs.
points.apply: Keep Sunday this week as a true day of rest and worship.

concl: Jesus forgives first, then heals.
Let us be carried, and let us carry others.
2027-01-15.resolve: Bring one friend to Jesus by prayer and invitation this week.

intro: Theme: “I have come to call not the righteous but sinners.”
The word that searches the heart and the mercy that welcomes the sinner.

q: Is not my word like fire, says the LORD, and like a hammer that breaks a rock in pieces?

Indeed, the word of God is living and active, sharper than any two-edged sword, piercing until it divides soul from spirit, joints from marrow; it is able to judge the thoughts and intentions of the heart.
points.apply: Pray with today's Gospel for ten minutes.

q: For I desire steadfast love and not sacrifice, the knowledge of God rather than burnt offerings.
When Jesus heard this, he said to them, “Those who are well have no need of a physician, but those who are sick; I have come to call not the righteous but sinners.”
points.apply: Welcome someone others avoid.

sub: Tested as we are, without sin.
q: As a father has compassion for his children, so the LORD has compassion for those who fear him.
Let us therefore approach the throne of grace with boldness, so that we may receive mercy and find grace to help in time of need.
points.apply: Go to confession with confidence.

concl: The word shows our sickness; the Physician heals it.
Come boldly: the throne is a throne of grace.
2027-01-16.resolve: Read one Gospel passage each day and let it search your heart.
